destination_or_phenomenon: The Liminal Arrivals Annex and its premature-reflection customs fault
summary: A municipal customs hall folds nine meters of tiled corridor into each millimeter of mirror silver, allowing a traveler's reflected sequence to reach inspection before the traveler's body crosses the room.
physics_or_metaphysical_rules: Reflected time advances only while the traveler's face is visible to silvered glass.
A premature reflection can perform one future decision but cannot improvise a second.
Leaving the mirror's ninety-degree viewing cone breaks borrowed identity authority.
history: The Annex opened as a pneumatic-mail terminal in Bureau Year 44.
Its mirrors were resurfaced with chronometric silver after a luggage duplication strike.
Form R-9 predates the official discovery of premature reflections by twelve years.
culture: Clerks congratulate delayed reflections and never acknowledge early ones directly.
Travelers leave one glove unreflected as a courtesy token.
architecture: Oxidized teal tile corridors narrow toward full-height smoked mirrors.
Brushed-aluminum ticket rails bend into impossible right angles without visible joints.
Amber CRT number boards hang from cream acoustic baffles.
materials: Mercury-bright mirror silver forms a visible two-millimeter meniscus at panel edges.
Floor tiles hold hairline black grout that continues straight inside reflections even when the room bends.
Forms use salmon paper with graphite fibers that do not appear in mirrors.
weather: Indoor condensation moves upward across the glass every forty-seven seconds.
A dry ozone draft emerges from closed inspection windows.
scale: Human-height customs mirrors contain corridor depth measured in kilometers.
A palm-sized R-9 form casts a shadow wider than the traveler when reflected.
transportation: Travelers arrive on a rubber-belt walkway moving at one walking pace.
Reflections arrive on a mirrored belt moving one decision ahead.
creatures_and_entities: Premature reflections retain the traveler's outline but initiate gestures one beat early.
Clerks appear only as gloved hands behind ribbed glass.
traveler_customs: Keep one shoulder outside the mirror's viewing cone.
Answer clerk questions only after the reflection closes its mouth.
taboos: Never wave at a waiting reflection.
Never compare badge dates while facing silvered glass.
bureaucratic_requirements: Form R-9 must be presented edge-first.
Three independent blinks must be recorded before identity release.
reasons_to_visit: The Annex offers the shortest transfer between incompatible timelines.
Its duty-free kiosk sells objects that cast yesterday's shadows.

locations_or_states.name: Rubber-Belt Arrival Walkway
locations_or_states.observable_geometry: A twelve-meter corridor telescopes by one tile whenever the amber counter changes.
locations_or_states.material_behavior: Cream rubber ridges move forward while their mirror image remains stationary.

locations_or_states.name: Mirror Customs Hall
locations_or_states.observable_geometry: Nine full-height panels form a shallow arc but reflect a straight kilometer-long terminal.
locations_or_states.material_behavior: Chronometric silver beads along the lower edge like cold mercury.

locations_or_states.name: Form R-9 Inspection Desk
locations_or_states.observable_geometry: A waist-high aluminum counter has a drawer opening visible only in reflection.
locations_or_states.material_behavior: Salmon paper stays matte while graphite fibers flash white under the blink verifier.

locations_or_states.name: Identity Holding Gallery
locations_or_states.observable_geometry: Rows of empty chrome chairs continue upward along the wall as if gravity turned ninety degrees.
locations_or_states.material_behavior: Each vinyl seat retains the heat outline of a person not yet seated.

survival_instructions: Do not greet a reflection already facing you.
Step sideways until no silvered surface contains both eyes.
Count three blinks that the reflection does not anticipate.
Present Form R-9 without allowing paper or fingers to touch glass.
soundscape: Rubber walkway ribs produce a muted 6-hertz thrum.
CRT relays click one beat before numbers change.
Reflections make no footstep but emit a reversed coat-rustle.
iconic_thumbnail_image: From behind the traveler, the smoked mirror shows the same figure already seated beneath amber number 001, looking back over one shoulder.
unresolved_lore: A Bureau badge in the final reflection bears a date preceding the Annex.
Inspection Window 0 appears on floor plans but not in the physical hall.
